law: No concept may exist without ownership. No overlap may exist between constitutional domains. No cross-domain ownership permitted.
dependencyLaw: Identity -> Knowledge -> Relationships -> Context -> Policy -> Trust -> Projection. Forbidden: circular dependencies, mutual ownership, cross-domain state mutation.
communication: All cross-domain communication occurs exclusively through explicit contracts. No domain may access another domain's internals.

boundaries.projectionLaw: Products, services, offers, subscriptions, contracts are projections. No projection may own truth. Truth belongs only to constitutional domains.

categories.name: Constitution
categories.covers: The laws, amendments and certification law that govern every other category.

categories.name: Meaning
categories.covers: What exists, what it is called, and what is known about it.

categories.name: Reality and Reasoning
categories.covers: How reality is observed, evidenced, explained, simulated and changed.

categories.name: Universal Dimensions
categories.covers: The coordinates any fact is placed in: where, when, how much, what value, in which expression, in what context.

categories.name: Structure
categories.covers: How declarations are stored once and linked.

categories.name: Decision and Control
categories.covers: Who may decide, under which policy and rule, and what was decided.

categories.name: Assurance
categories.covers: Protection, computed trust, the immutable record, and obligations.

categories.name: Interaction
categories.covers: How people see, are told, converse and find.

categories.name: Automation
categories.covers: How work runs: events, state, workflows, agents and connections.

categories.name: Intelligence
categories.covers: Measurement of the platform and the business.

categories.name: Platform
categories.covers: Storing, running, verifying, holding content and offering the platform.

categories.name: Business
categories.covers: Business projections composed from the domains; they own no truth.

laws.name: Zero Hard Coding
laws.statement: Only the immutable kernel is fixed in code. No business concept — product, service, offer, subscription, contract, industry, category, brand, country, currency, language, marketplace, store, tenant, organisation, person — is modelled as a primitive or a schema type; each is a projection of primitives, and the projection changes as context changes.

laws.name: Knowledge Once
laws.statement: Every concept, fact and capability is defined once, in one canonical source, with one owner. There are no parallel definitions, no conflicting truth, no orphans, and every code module has one home.

laws.name: Projection Law
laws.statement: Truth lives in the registry. Documents, business objects and reality are projections derived from it, never authored and never a second source; everything that can be derived is derived, not stored.

laws.name: Constitutional Governance
laws.statement: Every capability, change, evolution and autonomous action is governed; no execution bypasses governance.

laws.name: Explainability
laws.statement: Every action answers what happened, why, who authorised it, which policy allowed it, what evidence supports it, what confidence exists and what alternatives were evaluated.

laws.name: Configuration Over Code
laws.statement: Behaviour is driven by metadata, ontologies, policies, rules, registries and configuration, never by product-specific code. Launching anywhere, extending or changing the platform is configuration that a person with the manual, or an agent, can do from the console or the API.
aliases: Everything Is Configurable From The Console

laws.name: Single Ownership And Contract
laws.statement: No concept exists without an owner, no capability without a boundary, no boundary without a contract, no contract without governance; no term has two meanings, no meaning two definitions, and no two domains overlap.

laws.name: Independent Authorities
laws.statement: No entity owns another domain's concern — identity, geography, time, value, security, knowledge, intelligence, analytics or governance. It relates to them: a place stores no currency, a store stores no country.
enforcedBy: test/places.js (a place's currency and locale are settings owned by Value and Expression; a country row holds only the place)
test/stores.js (a store serves a set of places; its country is its jurisdiction, a Party setting)

laws.name: Dependency Law
laws.statement: Dependencies run Identity → Knowledge → Relationships → Context → Policy → Trust → Projection. Circular dependencies, mutual ownership and cross-domain state mutation are forbidden.

laws.name: Runtime Responsibility
laws.statement: The constitution defines truth, domains manage truth, the runtime derives reality, agents execute reality and applications consume it.

laws.name: Architectural Freeze
laws.statement: Primitives, domain ownership, contract structure and the governance, dependency and projection models are frozen. Change happens through registries, policies, capabilities, contexts, relationships, knowledge, agents and projections, never by adding primitives, and only through a recorded amendment.

laws.name: Generated Platform
laws.statement: Everything is generated from declarations: data models, APIs, interfaces, workflows, state machines, reports, dashboards, permissions, integrations, documentation, SDKs and tests. One generated API serves everyone — the console, storefronts, apps, agents, partners — with no private back door.

laws.name: Registry First
laws.statement: Everything is discoverable: if it exists it is registered, describable and searchable.

laws.name: Infinite Extensibility
laws.statement: Every domain is complete from zero to infinite and assumes no Earth, country, calendar, value unit, language or text direction. New kinds, places, categories and domains arrive by registration and configuration, never redesign; every concept is self-governing, self-describing, self-registering, self-validating, self-certifying, composable, replaceable and independently evolvable.

laws.name: Technology Agnostic
laws.statement: Nothing depends on a vendor, database, cloud or framework; each is an adapter chosen by configuration, per domain or per tenant.

laws.name: Contextual Distribution
laws.statement: Configuring a place projects what applies there — expression, value units, tax, compliance, catalogue, pricing — inherited down the place hierarchies, for any number of places at once.

laws.name: Platform-Owned Master Data
laws.statement: Master data belongs to the platform. Platforms, tenants and modules select it through views and never copy it; a tenant extends only within its own scope.

laws.name: Selection From Owners
laws.statement: Every choice offered anywhere is a selection from the domain that owns the subject, in any combination. Constraints are declared by the entities, and every option carries a free or paid offering.

laws.name: Nothing Invented
laws.statement: Creating one thing never creates another. Anything missing shows as incomplete until a person or agent completes it; nothing is filled with a placeholder.
enforcedBy: test/places.js (no place invented above the countries)

laws.name: Rules Belong To Kinds
laws.statement: A format or validation rule belongs to the kind that needs it, never to a whole domain.
enforcedBy: lib/kernel.js (attribute values checked against the type their kind declares)

laws.name: One Kernel
laws.statement: Every domain is built on the same kernel and receives every kernel part and shared service; no domain can lack one.

laws.name: Bounded Agents
laws.statement: An agent is a party with declared permissions, scope, budget and audit; it never exceeds the person or role it acts for, and money or irreversible actions need declared approval.

laws.name: Security Floor
laws.statement: Security and compliance are on by default; a tenant or operator may tighten policy but never weaken it below the platform baseline.

laws.name: Immutable Record
laws.statement: Every change and every access to sensitive data is recorded in an append-only, hash-chained record that no one can edit.
enforcedBy: lib/kernel.js and test/kernel.js (the kernel's hash-chained event log)

laws.name: Packages Compose
laws.statement: Packages compose domains into ready-made, editable platforms; a customisation is an overlay that survives every package upgrade.

laws.name: Every Law Is Enforced
laws.statement: A law without an executable check is not finished; the register records each law's enforcement, and the count of laws not yet enforced may only fall.

kernel.name: Kinds
kernel.statement: The kinds a domain contains, each declaring its attributes, where it may sit, its validation rules, its identifier schemes and whether it carries a shape. Users add kinds.

kernel.name: Nodes
kernel.statement: The instances of every kind, with no limit on count or depth.

kernel.name: Hierarchies
kernel.statement: Named hierarchies over shared nodes; a node may sit in many, and in more than one place within one.

kernel.name: Identifiers
kernel.statement: A universal ID for every node, plus any number of code schemes, declared as data.

kernel.name: Shape
kernel.statement: A point, area or volume in a declared coordinate system; any coordinate resolves to every node that contains it.
kernel.note: any declared coordinate system; point, box (across a wrapping seam), ball and polygon; containment scans every shape in a system (no spatial index yet) and polygons are planar on the first two axes

kernel.name: Attributes
kernel.statement: Typed values declared in the registry; text is multilingual through Expression, sensitive values are encrypted through Security.

kernel.name: Versions
kernel.statement: Bi-temporal history: valid time and recorded time; nothing is overwritten and any past state can be queried.

kernel.name: Events
kernel.statement: One event log that every change and declared occurrence is written to; workflows, notifications, analytics, webhooks and audit read it.
kernel.note: the kernel's log is hash-chained; audit_log and the webhook bus (lib/events.js) are not yet merged into it (GAP-27)

kernel.name: Change Lifecycle
kernel.statement: Draft, validate, preview, approve, publish (now or scheduled), roll back; hide is reversible; delete is archive, then purge with a separate permission.
kernel.note: changes are drafted as data and validated, previewed, approved (with the approve permission, by someone other than the author), published now or on schedule and rolled back; nodes hide (left out of every listing), archive and purge with a separate permission. Purge cannot remove codes already written in earlier event payloads, because the log is never edited

kernel.name: Views
kernel.statement: A platform, tenant, module or subscriber selects hierarchies, subtrees, depth, groupings and labels by reference, never by copy.

kernel.name: Scope
kernel.statement: Every declaration lives in a namespace (platform, tenant, publisher) and at a scope level (platform, tenant, store, channel, place, language, segment, device type, person).

kernel.name: Resolution
kernel.statement: One resolver answers what applies here and now from relationships, hierarchies (nearest wins), time windows, context and rules; settings and defaults are its answers, not stored copies.
kernel.note: one resolver: nearest assignment up each hierarchy, profiles order hierarchies, namespaces most specific first, the answer says where it came from; time windows apply, rules (Rule) are not yet an input

buildStatuses.means: declared and contracted, with no code and no live route yet; its contract's APIs are designed interfaces
owns code or live routes, but not everything its contract describes
everything its contract describes runs, and its laws are enforced

amendments.summary: The kernel's read side runs. Shape (K05, lib/kernel-shape.js): coordinate systems are data (axes, bounds, wrapping), shapes have valid time, and any coordinate resolves to every node that contains it, from a site to a galaxy. Scope and resolution (K11, K12, lib/kernel-context.js): a setting is declared once, assigned in a namespace at any scope node, and one resolver answers what applies here and now — nearest wins, profiles order hierarchies, every answer says where it came from, and nothing assigned stays unresolved. Views (K10): subtrees selected by reference and computed live. Namespaces carry their holder (tenant:42); kinds and hierarchies not declared in a namespace are the platform's. CI could not run on 3e67d62 because the GitHub account's billing blocked the jobs (GAP-29).

amendments.summary: The kernel's change lifecycle runs (K09, lib/kernel-lifecycle.js). A change is a list of kernel operations written as data; it is validated and previewed by dry runs that leave nothing behind, approved by someone other than its author, published now or at a scheduled time, and rolled back by closing what it recorded and reopening what it superseded — refused while a later change still builds on it. A node hides (reversibly), archives, and is purged only when archived and only with the separate purge permission, leaving a tombstone event. States, transitions, operations and the permission are data (lib/seed/kernel.json → lifecycle). Every kernel part now runs; none is fully built.

Kernel follow-ups. Hidden and archived nodes drop out of every kernel listing — node lists, children, subtrees, views and coordinate lookups — unless a caller asks for them; paths, ancestors and history keep the whole structure, and hiding a node does not hide what sits under it. Approving a change needs the declared approve permission, which the caller is granted by Authority; the kernel checks grants, never role names. Node states moved into the kernel's own tables.
changes: lib/kernel-shape.js, lib/kernel-context.js: listings leave out hidden nodes

amendments.summary: P09 begins: places are on the kernel. Every country and subdivision is a node of the place kind (declared as data in lib/seed/places.json) in one place tree — countries at the top, nothing invented above them, subdivisions under their country or parent subdivision to any depth — with its code as an identifier in its declared scheme and its row's universal ID as its own. lib/places.js mirrors the master after every write and on every boot: a rename is a new version, a switched-off country is hidden, a re-parented subdivision moves with its past kept, a deleted row is archived; a warm pass writes nothing. The tables remain the source until the writes move onto the kernel.
changes: lib/kernel.js: createNode adopts an existing universal ID; placementsOf; writes take the lock up front
lib/registry.js reconcileDerived, lib/entity.js propagate, lib/global.js country writes: mirror the place tree

amendments.summary: A place's currency and locale are no longer facts of the place. They are settings owned by Value and Expression (declared in lib/seed/places.json), assigned at the place's node on the kernel and answered by the resolver — so a subdivision inherits its country's currency, and a setting assigned at a subdivision applies there and below. registry.country(), through which the platform's readers ask, answers currency and locale from the kernel and a country's money symbol and decimals from its currency in Value's master; a country profile's tax is the tax engine's rule, no longer the country's legacy tax columns. The master's columns remain as the mirror's input until the writes move onto the kernel.

amendments.summary: Every application write to a place goes to the kernel first. The entity engine's built-in entities may name their owner's write path (lib/seed/entity.json WRITERS; tenant-defined entities cannot): the country and subdivision entities name Geo's, which records the change on the kernel and writes the row in one transaction — a write the row refuses leaves the kernel untouched, a write the kernel refuses never reaches the row. global.js's country writes and the platform's country withdrawal take the same path; a deleted place is archived with its history; a country row carries its place's universal ID. The boot mirror remains for seeds and legacy rows.

amendments.summary: The kernel is the record for places. The registry's first-boot seeding of countries, its repair of legacy and newly declared countries, and its materialisation of a country's subdivisions all go through Geo's write path, so every place is recorded on the kernel in the same transaction as its row. The boot mirror becomes an import: it creates places only for rows the kernel has never seen (an install that predates the place tree), under its own actor, and never changes a place that exists. A write that bypasses the write path no longer reaches the place tree.

Its currency and locale exist only as Value's and Expression's settings at its place on the kernel, its money symbol and decimals are its currency's, and its tax is the tax engine's. amendments.summary: A store stores no country. Every store is a node of the store kind (owner Party), known by its store id, with its row's universal ID. The places it serves are a relationship of their own (owner Relationship): in the serves hierarchy a store sits under each place it serves — any mix of countries and subdivisions — each with a time window. Its jurisdiction is a Party setting at its node naming one of those places; settings, tax, billing, modules, the global console and the offer engine's context read the store's country from it, and a subdivision jurisdiction answers the country it lies in. Saving a store's country moves its jurisdiction and the settings row keeps no copy. A fresh install's store row has no country column; an older install's stores are imported at boot (what the storefront showed, else the row's column, else provisioning policy) and the column is never read again. A deleted store's node is archived with its history; a country a store serves cannot be deleted.

amendments.summary: P11: Time owns time. Calendars, chronologies, temporal units and their conversions are Time's registries (lib/seed/time.json), not lists in the offer engine; rows an operator added under the engine's old list names join Time's once. A place's time zone is Time's setting at the place, resolved up the place tree like its calendar: each seeded country has its primary zone, any subdivision, city or colony may have its own, and a place under none is in the declared default zone. A zone the host's clock knows answers the local date, weekday and hour at an instant; a colony's own clock is carried as declared. The offer engine's temporal context carries the zone where the exchange happens (the request's, the place's, else the store's jurisdiction's) and its local time.

amendments.summary: An idle keep-alive connection outlives a load balancer's idle timeout: the server's keep-alive is 65 s by default (LX_KEEPALIVE_MS), so the balancer, not the server, closes it. With Node's 5 s default the server closed idle sockets while a client was about to reuse one, which reset the client's next request — the cause of the intermittent ECONNRESET in the test suites (GAP-28), and of 502s behind a balancer. Shutdown closes the listening server, TLS included. A security-suite crash now prints the server's last words and the network cause.
changes: server.js: keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout; shutdown closes the listening server
test/security.js: a crash reports its cause and the server's stderr

amendments.summary: P12 begins: Expression speaks languages by configuration. Languages are a registry naming each one's script and writing direction (lib/seed/expression.json); the storefront's shipped copy is the source language, and the message catalogue (the messages table, the console's message entity) holds it in Arabic, Hindi, Spanish, French and German. A request is answered in the language it names, else the shopper's remembered choice, else the best one the browser asks for, else the store's locale's language, else the source — always one the platform can speak. The storefront sets the page's language and direction, so a right-to-left language lays out right to left, and offers a language switch. A store's own saved copy applies in its own language only; an operator's catalogue edit survives the seed. Bug fixed: the store import failed when the settings module was what first booted the database (a circular load).

amendments.summary: The platform runs on Postgres, and is checked there end to end. The Postgres client opened a new connection for every statement, so no transaction held (a BEGIN, its statements and its COMMIT or ROLLBACK each ran on a different connection), the migration could not roll back, and a busy server exhausted its ports; it authenticated only with md5 or cleartext, not SCRAM-SHA-256 (Postgres's default and what managed Postgres requires), and a TLS connection wrote to a closed socket. Now one persistent connection serves the db bridge and a migration: SCRAM-SHA-256, TLS upgraded in place, one statement at a time, and a connection lost inside a transaction refuses every statement until the caller's ROLLBACK. The migration quotes reserved column names, keeps any identity column (the kernel's seq) and SQLite's implicit rowid (which subdivisions point at), declares TEXT a numeric column that holds text, translates indexes on their own, and runs in one transaction that stops at its first error. The dialect translator learned IFNULL, last_insert_rowid(), strftime and date() of stored text timestamps, datetime('now', ?), typed concatenation parameters and multi-row INSERT OR IGNORE. Queries fixed to be portable: GROUP BY lists, HAVING on aggregates, an unaliased day, IS ? on a parameter. Three latent bugs found by sweeping every SELECT through Postgres, broken on SQLite too: a store's providers on the global console read columns tenant_gateways never had, a shipment's third-party push looked up a column that does not exist (so it never ran), and a supplier's minimum order looked up a SKU column product_suppliers does not have. scripts/pg-check.js (npm run check:postgres) migrates a fresh install, checks the kernel's transactions, places, stores, time, expression and Value, and loads every page and console section with the server on Postgres; CI runs it against a SCRAM-authenticated Postgres 16 service. CI moves to the actions' Node 24 runtime on a pinned ubuntu-24.04 runner.
changes: lib/pgworker.js: one connection; a broken transaction refuses until ROLLBACK
lib/pgbridge.js: the identity column an INSERT returns; an ignored insert returns no id without failing

amendments.summary: The platform master and configuration by selection, adopted as design (GLOBAL_MASTER.md). Every product and service is an entity in the platform master, of a kind declared as a row and classified in any number of hierarchies of any depth; codes, scientific names and local codes are identifiers under identifier schemes; what the source model called columns are attributes on kinds, inherited down a hierarchy and applicable by context. A platform sees the master through its permissions (scope, objects, actions, review) as a projection, with its overlays held in its own scope; nothing is copied. Every platform addition, modification or retirement is a contribution: the platform master's owner reviews each one, and once approved applies it, adds it as new, or attaches it as an addendum, or rejects it with a reason. A platform is configured through a blueprint's steps (official and working authorities, languages, value units, taxes, identifier schemes, selling model, what it sells, features, sites), every setting on its own with an effective time to the minute; discovery derives each capability as mandatory, recommended, added or requested with its reason, and requests are captured at configuration and editable by the platform owner afterwards. Platform kinds and blends stop deciding features and become starter packages. Fulfilment modes include appointment, chat, audio and video; media sessions are built in, with connectors plugged in beside them, and communication may itself be offered on any commercial terms. The starter master ships the maximum declared content. Steps P27–P30.
changes: _registry/terminology.json: Contribution, Addendum, Identifier Scheme, Fulfilment Mode, Discovery, Media Session; Overlay widened to the platform master

amendments.summary: Coverage of every type of platform, product, service, deal and offer, adopted as design (GLOBAL_MASTER.md sections 8–10). The coverage matrix names 32 types of platform by what they do (everything marketplaces, cross-border bargain marketplaces, hypermarket chains, wholesale exchanges, quick commerce, fresh and perishables grocery, online pharmacy and health, food delivery, fashion, electronics, furniture, automotive parts, digital goods, education, subscription boxes, services and consultancy, rentals, travel, ticketing, resale, auctions, group buying, live selling, reseller commerce, dropshipping, made-to-order, gifts, pre-orders, super apps, mobility, operations); each becomes a blueprint fixture that fails while any capability is left requested. The engines still missing and the offer types still missing (payment-instrument offers, instalments without cost, exchange, free gift, mix and match, lightning deals, sale events, clearance, price match, price-drop protection, member and tier prices, loyalty points, channel, time-window and place conditions, clipped coupons, two-sided referrals, gamified rewards, fee waivers) are listed as phase 9. Steps P31–P32.

Phase 1 of GLOBAL_MASTER.md: the kernel parts the platform master stands on are complete. K01: a kind may extend another (entity and sub-entity, any depth, no loops); it inherits attributes, identifier schemes, placement rules and root, and may add attributes or tighten an inherited one but never change its type; a placement rule, a view's kinds and a nodeKind reference accept every kind extending the one named; validation rules are declared per attribute from a registry of operators (min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, oneOf, nodeKind, unique, languages), each checked against the value types it applies to and its parameter when declared. K06: text in many languages is a value type (expression) whose languages come from the Expression registry, answered in the language asked, else the source language; an amount in a unit is a value type (quantity) whose unit is a node. K10: a view declares groupings (by kind, by an attribute, by the nearest ancestor of a kind in a hierarchy), nested in order, each declaring its parameters. K11: kinds, hierarchies, settings, resolution profiles and views may be declared at a scope node inside a namespace; a node created at a scope is checked against the scope's kind. Bug fixed: a namespace holder could not be a number, so a tenant namespace such as tenant:42 was refused; holders have their own declared pattern.
changes: lib/kernel.js: extends, effective kinds, isA, constraints, expression and quantity, text, scopes, holder pattern
lib/kernel-context.js: scoped declarations, view groupings, viewGroups
lib/seed/kernel.json: valueTypes, constraints, groupings, holderPattern, maxExtends

amendments.summary: Phase 2, first part, of GLOBAL_MASTER.md (P27): the platform master stands on the kernel. lib/platform-master.js writes the starter content of lib/seed/master.json into the kernel the first time the master is asked for anything, in one transaction and only what is missing: 54 kinds (classification levels from domain to model, the item kinds every product and service type extends, identifier schemes, dimensions and units, attribute definitions, vocabularies and terms), the trade taxonomy (998 nodes: domains, industries with the capabilities each requires and recommends, categories and subcategories), the tariff nomenclature's sections and chapters with their codes, 36 identifier schemes each declaring its format, check rule, authority and places, 18 dimensions and 82 units with conversion factors and offsets, 124 attribute definitions bound to taxonomy nodes, kinds and places, 14 relationship types each a hierarchy of its own, and vocabularies for item kinds, fulfilment modes (each with the capabilities it requires), lifecycle, media kinds, packaging levels, variant axes, shipping classes, roles and selling models. An item's attribute set is computed: a definition bound nowhere applies everywhere, one bound to taxonomy nodes applies under them, one bound to kinds applies to every kind extending them, one bound to places applies inside them; its facts are checked against that set with the kernel's one value check. The kernel now checks every code against its scheme's declaration (format, case, check digit: GS1, Luhn, ISBN, ISSN, CAS) and exposes checkValue and checkCode. Measure moves from designed to partial (units still duplicated in lib/meta.js until the vocabularies are projected from the master).
changes: lib/kernel.js: checkValue, checkCode, scheme declarations, check rules

amendments.summary: Phase 2, second part, of GLOBAL_MASTER.md (P27): the global catalogue is the platform master. The global_products table is gone: every global product is a master item — its code under the seller-code scheme, its multilingual title and description, its place in the trade taxonomy, its place among the product universes, its media, its lifecycle term and the profile the platform authors for stores — and lib/gcatalog.js only projects an item into the record the console edits and the store import copies, and writes such a record back as master writes (an edit is a new version; a delete retires the item, keeping its history). The product universes the registry declares are a classification of the master, and the kind each sells as is data on the kinds vocabulary (the universe-to-type constant in code is gone; an unmapped universe sells as the kind marked default; an entity named by the words of a universe or a kind resolves to it). The placeholder product the old seed wrote for every universe is gone: a universe is a classification, not a product. An install that predates the master moves every row onto it once, keeping code, place, universe, price, tax class, attributes, profile and status, re-points the store permissions and imported products that named it, and drops the table. Lifecycle states in the console come from the master; what an imported product starts with is platform policy (provisioning.importedProduct).
changes: lib/gcatalog.js: a projection over the master; the legacy move
lib/platform-master.js: universes from the registry, kindForUniverse, lifecycleTerm, move, update
lib/api.js: the global catalogue API on the master; categories from the master taxonomy

amendments.summary: Phase 2, third part, of GLOBAL_MASTER.md (P27): every product vocabulary the platform reads by name is answered by the platform master, and its copies are gone. The master's seed declares sixteen projections — product types, lifecycle and its transitions, media kinds, packaging levels, shipping classes, variant axes, roles, fulfilment modes, selling models, taxonomy levels (vocabularies), industries (the taxonomy's industry nodes with their domain), units and their conversions (from each unit's factor against its dimension's base unit), identity fields (the codes an item may carry) and relationship types (the relationship hierarchies) — and lib/registry.js answers each from the master, lists it for authoring beside its own lists, and writes a console save or removal to the master (a vocabulary term, an industry under its domain, a unit in its dimension, an identifier scheme that items may then carry, a relationship hierarchy). A list's default stays declared once, in lib/seed/defaults.json. An install that kept such a list as a registry row has the entries the master lacks added to it once, and the row goes. lib/meta.js no longer holds industries, product types, lifecycle, relationship types, media kinds, packaging levels, units, conversions, roles, identity fields, shipping classes, variant axes or taxonomy levels; the store seeders and modules read them through the registry. The universe a corpus entity names is matched by its words; a universe no kind names sells as the kind the vocabulary marks for it. Fixes: the database exports are visible before the bootstrap seeds its stores (seeding now reads the master, which reads the database); a scheme's places are held as codes and resolved when asked, so a scheme written before the place tree loads still names its places.
changes: lib/platform-master.js: projections, saves, retirement, adoption, live relationship types
lib/registry.js: the master's lists answered, authored and adopted
lib/db.js: exports before bootstrap; seeders read the registry

amendments.summary: Phase 3 and 4 of GLOBAL_MASTER.md (P28): permissions on the platform master, contributions and their review, addenda. A permission (lib/master-permissions.js, owner Authority) is a node of the master: its holder (a namespace), the master nodes it covers (each with everything under it in the trade taxonomy and the product universes; none: the whole master), the objects and actions it allows (an action implies the actions its term names: select implies view, sell implies select), the attributes the holder sees and when the holder's changes are reviewed. It is revoked by recording so from an instant on, so what it allowed before stays answerable. A store's access to a global product is a permission at one of the master's access levels (none, read, list, sell, full); the store_product_config table is gone — an install that kept it has each row moved onto a permission at the same level, and the table dropped. A platform never writes the master: what it proposes (add, modify, overlay, retire) is a contribution (lib/master-contributions.js, owner Evolution) the global platform reviews — approved and placed (applied to the master as a new version; added as a new entity; attached as an addendum for the platforms and places named, a retirement so placed hiding the entity there) or rejected with a reason; its author never reviews it. Reviewed before, nothing changes until approval; reviewed after, it holds at once for the proposing platform only, as a provisional addendum or a provisional entity the review places or withdraws. What a platform sees of an entity is the master with the addenda for it (and its place) over it, cut to the attributes its permission shows; a store imports a global product as it sees it. The actions, objects, review modes, access levels, contribution actions and placements are master vocabularies; the life of a contribution is the contribution state machine. Platform console: Master Review (approve with a placement or reject with a reason) and Master Permissions (grant and revoke by platform). Store console: Master Contributions (its permissions, its proposals, propose and withdraw). Fix: the store-access screen sent a product's id as a number, which item ids are not.
changes: lib/gcatalog.js: the gate and the import on permissions and the store's view
lib/api.js: master tree, vocabularies, permissions, contributions and review routes; store access on permissions
lib/db.js: store_product_config removed from the schema
public/js/platform.js: Master Review, Master Permissions; access levels from the master

amendments.summary: Phase 5 of GLOBAL_MASTER.md (P29): a platform is configured by answering its setup steps, and discovery decides its capabilities. The steps are the master's blueprint_steps vocabulary — official jurisdiction, working jurisdictions, languages, currencies, taxes, identity types, selling model, what it sells, how it delivers, features switched on, recommended features switched off, features requested, sites — each naming its answer, where its options come from, whether many may be chosen and whether it must be answered (lib/platform-setup.js). Each answer is its own setting on the kernel in the platform's namespace, effective from the minute it is given for (DEC-018); what has come due is applied, at once or by the server's sweep each minute: the jurisdiction moves and the places served follow, the currency, language and tax mode follow, the platform's permission on the master covers what it sells at the setup's access level, and discovery (lib/platform-discovery.js) classes every capability — mandatory (something chosen requires it: a taxonomy node and everything above it, an item kind, a fulfilment mode the platform chose, its selling model, a rule of a jurisdiction where it trades), recommended (something chosen recommends it, or a fulfilment mode its kinds can use but it did not choose), added (switched on with no cause) or requested (no capability atom provides it yet) — each with its reasons. Mandatory and recommended capabilities are switched on, a declined recommendation off, and what was requested is kept for the platform owner to edit (DEC-019). Platform kinds and their blends are starter packages: a kind pre-fills setup answers (its selling model, what it sells, how it delivers, its blend's features, its jurisdiction's currency and language), every one editable; a registration that gives answers is provisioned from them (a shopfront when it sells anything under a selling model with one, shipping and a warehouse when it delivers something physical) rather than from its kind (DEC-021). Selling models, the jurisdictions' rules and the discovery classes are master vocabularies. Platform console: Platform Setup (answer the steps, the minute they take effect, discovery's preview with reasons, requests).
changes: lib/api.js: setup steps, discovery preview, a platform's answers and requests; registration through the steps
lib/seed/master.json, lib/seed/meta.json: starter answers per kind
